primitives.name: Stability Recipe
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT the stability recipe (noise augmentation on conditioning frames + teacher-forcing training with autoregressive evaluation) is the definitive answer to compounding error in autoregressive simulators; GSE's game simulator must adopt it.
primitives.assumptions: Autoregressive error propagation is mitigated through noise-injected conditioning and supervised training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When conditioning frames lack noise augmentation, divergence accumulates beyond 64 steps.

layer2.mapping: Noise augmentation in GSE mimics Bayesian prior regularization, stabilizing latent-space dynamics against sampling drift.

primitives.name: Latent State Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The visual-diffusion machinery itself is less relevant (GSE simulates structured state, not pixels), but the PERSISTENCE result (game state like health/ammo tallies survive long trajectories) validates latent-state simulation.
primitives.assumptions: Structured game states persist reliably over long sequences without pixel-level fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pixel-based models fail when simulating long-term state consistency.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses latent-space diffusion to encode and predict structured game variables (health, ammo) rather than image pixels.
layer2.telemetry: Persistence of game state metrics (e.g., health) across 64+ steps.

primitives.name: Interactive World Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Interactive World Simulation formalism (§2): simulation distribution q(o_n | o_{<n}, a_{≤n}); objective minimizes E[D(o_q, o_p)] under the agent's policy, with conditioning observations from the environment (teacher forcing) or from the simulation (autoregressive).
primitives.latex: q(o_n | o_{<n}, a_{\leq n}) \text{ with } D(o_q, o_p) \text{ as divergence metric}

primitives.assumptions: Simulation distribution is conditionally Markovian and optimizable via divergence minimization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when environmental observations are misaligned with simulated dynamics.

layer2.mapping: GSE's simulation distribution mirrors the probabilistic world model used in reinforcement learning.
layer2.telemetry: PSNR/LPIPS on teacher-forced and autoregressive rollouts.

The core insight is that diffusion models can be repurposed for real-time game simulation by conditioning on structured state sequences. The stability recipe ensures that errors do not compound over time by injecting noise into conditioning inputs during training, which forces the model to learn robust recovery mechanisms. This is critical because autoregressive prediction inherently suffers from error accumulation. The latent-state simulation primitive validates that structured game variables (like health or ammo) remain consistent over long trajectories, supporting the use of latent representations instead of pixel-level modeling. The interactive world simulation formalism defines the probabilistic structure of the game state evolution, where the objective function minimizes divergence between simulated and real-world observations. These primitives together form a coherent framework for building stable, high-fidelity game simulators.
